chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Akhi Fudayl, from Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man from whom comes out something similar to a pumpkin seed, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ablution upon him.' And it is reported that if it is stained with faeces, he must repeat the ablution.

key_terms.حَبِّ الْقَرْعِ: Pumpkin seed (referring to the size/shape of the discharge)

ai.seo_question: Does discharge similar to a pumpkin seed break wudu according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between minor impurities that do not nullify wudhu, such as mazi (pre-seminal fluid), and those that do, specifically when mixed with faecal matter (adha). It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the mere presence of a small amount of discharge does not break ablution unless it is accompanied by a specific impurity or sufficient quantity, highlighting the practical ease intended in ritual purity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Akhay Fuzayl, from Fuzayl, from, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the man from whom comes out similar to a seed. Heasws said: ‘There is no Ablution (Wudhu) upon him’. And it is reported that when (such things) are stained with the faeces, repeat the Ablution (Wudhu)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Hassan ibn Akhiy Fudayl from Fudayl who has said the following: “It is about the case of a man from whose buttocks such things like pumpkin seed may come out. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘It is not necessary for him to take Wudu’.’”
